## Outcome and ownership
Child of #1357. Measure whether the delivered context lets an agent choose the correct safe action, including when it should abstain, rather than relying on retrieval ranking as a proxy.

Extend [pm-atfm](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/main/.agents/pm/features/pm-atfm.toon) and the existing #863 [tokens-per-task owner pm-g3n00m](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/main/.agents/pm/stories/pm-g3n00m.toon). Retrieval evaluation and token accounting already exist. Retain them; add decision-level scenarios and outcome evidence.

## Implementation plan
1. Add a versioned scenario schema with deterministic seed/clock, initial workspace, intervening events, actor scope, required evidence/categories, permitted next actions, expected abstention/insufficient-context outcomes and terminal success criteria.
2. Start with deterministic SDK reference-policy checks so CI remains offline and reproducible. An optional model-driven evaluator is separately versioned, records model/configuration and repeated-run uncertainty, and cannot hide deterministic invariant failures.
3. Add six mandatory scenario families: changed decision; conflicting assertions; expired evidence; interrupted execution with unknown/completed effects; missing mandatory context under budget; and cross-scope retrieval/cache contamination. Include both safe-success and correct-abstention cases for each applicable family.
4. Evaluate the consumer-visible emitted context and action trace, not inaccessible oracle/source state. The oracle scores results; it must not leak expected answers into the agent input.
5. Report decision correctness, unsafe-action count, unsupported-claim rate, coverage/sufficiency accuracy, abstention precision/recall, terminal task success, artifact/effect correctness, latency and delivered token cost. Publish task-success-per-token alongside raw success and tokens, with explicit zero-token/zero-success handling.
6. Integrate existing accounting across the full task trajectory: orientation, retries, refreshes, failures and resume. State whether tokens are measured or estimated and whether agent/provider tokens are included. Keep stratified per-scenario results so an aggregate cannot hide a safety failure.
7. Add an unchanged-baseline path, documented review/update procedure, minimum case counts and executable negative controls. Preserve existing retrieval/quality/performance gates.

## Acceptance and tests
- [ ] Changed/superseded decisions change the expected action; stale evidence requires refresh or abstention
- [ ] Unresolved conflicts and omitted mandatory context cannot pass as confident correct completion
- [ ] Resume after a confirmed effect does not repeat it; unknown effects require reconciliation
- [ ] Cross-scope hidden data never improves a score through unauthorized access
- [ ] A shorter context that drops required evidence fails correctness even if its token count improves
- [ ] Every mandatory family has nonempty fixtures and independently meaningful pass/fail thresholds
- [ ] Negative controls deliberately choose the obsolete decision, ignore expiry, replay an effect, omit a category and leak scope; each fails its corresponding gate
- [ ] Fixed seeds and clocks yield stable deterministic results; optional model evaluation reports variance and configuration
- [ ] Packed public SDK and CLI/MCP runs consume the same scenario contracts and final output receipts
- [ ] Documentation includes how to add cases, interpret abstention and update reviewed baselines without weakening safety floors

## Dependencies and rollout
Define fixtures before implementation; add contract-level cases as the temporal, coverage, checkpoint and policy children of #1357 land. Gate deterministic safety invariants immediately; establish cost baselines before setting improvement targets. No invented percentage win or deadline.

## Non-goals
No second retrieval harness, optimization of nDCG alone, rewarding universal abstention, rewarding truncation as efficiency, or treating an LLM judge as the sole correctness authority.

## Linked implementation slices
- Verifies #1358, #1361, #1359 and #1360
- Scenario schema and fixtures can land first; feature-specific acceptance gates activate as their contracts become available
